correctness.rationale: Self-contained exact update analysis proves fixed states, hub-preserving and hub-switching two-cycles, a necessary-and-sufficient no-isolated-one and strict-majority characterization, plus a two-ring parity split. The cyclic-run polynomial is counted both via three-state trace and binomial compositions. A symmetric strict potential proves period at most two. Finite checker verifies 262128 wheel states and direct transfer/run identities, with no finite-to-infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The complete wheel-specific hub-switching criterion and parity-split weighted cyclic-run census are absent from the checked closest primary sources: the historical cycle rule has no universal hub, general majority results establish period or convergence rather than wheel counts, tree classifications exclude wheel cycles, and max/minterm or XOR systems have different Boolean operators. The preceding ladder majority census applies to an edge-disjoint graph family with no global threshold hub. Indexed searches cannot establish absolute uniqueness; residual risks are stated.
residual_risks: A preexisting wheel-specific attractor enumeration may be indexed under another graph/name or appear in an inaccessible thesis or older source; a literature search cannot establish absolute uniqueness.

value.rationale: The exact wheel orbit census solves an intrinsically motivated dynamical invariant of the simplest ring-plus-hub network. It exhibits exactly two steady states but exponentially many oscillatory attractors, a hub-oscillation parity bifurcation, and a sharp small-size threshold; the separate structural hub reduction is not a routine restatement of ring fixed-point enumeration. Basin counts and the optimal growth rate are not claimed.
